s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent episodes of abdominal pain and syncope following alcohol ingestion with a prolonged time course
salient_findings: Recurrent abdominal pain after alcohol ingestion
High-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions on ECG
key_facts: Patient presented with recurrent abdominal pain and syncope
Symptoms occurred 6-20 hours after alcohol ingestion
Symptoms lasted 5-10 minutes
Syncope occurred only after large alcohol intake
Patient has a history of hypertension
Patient has a history of smoking and alcohol overconsumption
High-sensitivity troponin I was normal
Serum potassium was normal
ECG showed high-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions
ECG showed ST segment elevations in leads II, III, and aVF
Coronary angiography showed 10% stenosis in proximal LAD and RCA

shortlist.label: Alcoholic cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of long-term alcohol overconsumption and presented with symptoms consistent with cardiac dysfunction

shortlist.label: Vasovagal syncope
shortlist.why_kept: Patient experienced syncope after large alcohol intake, which could trigger a vasovagal response

shortlist.label: Alcohol-induced autonomic dysfunction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms, including abdominal pain and syncope, could be related to autonomic dysfunction caused by chronic alcohol use

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: ECG findings showed premature ventricular contractions and high-degree atrioventricular block, which could be indicative of an underlying arrhythmogenic condition

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms, including abdominal pain and syncope, could be related to a stress-induced cardiomyopathy, such as Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, potentially triggered by alcohol consumption

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of recurrent abdominal pain and syncope occurring 6-20 hours after alcohol ingestion, lasting 5-10 minutes, and worsening with large alcohol intake, are consistent with alcohol-induced autonomic dysfunction, which can cause orthostatic hypotension and syncope due to impaired autonomic regulation.

rejected.label: Alcoholic cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of alcohol overconsumption, the coronary angiography showed minimal stenosis and the high-sensitivity troponin I was normal, making cardiomyopathy less likely.

rejected.label: Vasovagal syncope
rejected.why: Vasovagal syncope typically occurs in response to specific triggers such as stress or pain, and is not directly related to alcohol ingestion.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The ECG findings did not specifically indicate right ventricular involvement, and the patient's symptoms are not typical of this condition.

rejected.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and ECG findings do not match the typical presentation of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, which is often triggered by emotional or physical stress and has distinct ECG and echocardiographic features.
